# Incident Report — MTA 2024-08-15 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## 1. Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** |
| Windows domain | LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG (workgroup NetBIOS: LAFONTAINEBLEU) |
| Logged-in Windows user | **plucero** (confirmed via Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ CNameString, realm LAFONTAINEBLEU.ORG, against DC 10.8.15.4 / WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS) |

Source: DHCP (Option 12 hostname), NBNS name registration, and Kerberos ticket exchanges all consistently identify the same host/user.

## 2. Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed.** No IDS/Suricata/AV export was present in the evidence directory (only the raw pcap), so there is no signature hit to cite. The behavioral chain and artifact strings support classifying this as a **generic HTTP-based loader/backdoor**, internal build name **"knock"** (from an embedded PDB path in the payload DLL: `E:\work\ooooooops\181\knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`, PE export name `release.dll`). It is delivered through a fake-invoice/fake-FedEx phishing kit (ZIP → obfuscated JScript downloader → DLL loader). This does not match a publicly-named commodity family I can confirm from the traffic alone — I am not asserting a specific malware-family brand name (e.g., "X" RAT/loader) since that would require signature or sample matching not available in this evidence set.

## 3. Infection Timeline (relative to capture start)

| T+ | Event |
|---|---|
| 71.4s | DNS query for `quote.checkfedexexp.com` |
| 74.68s | `GET quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?...` (Chrome/Edge 127 UA) → HTTP 200, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="Invoice 876597035_003.zip"`, served from Cloudflare-fronted 104.21.55.70 |
| ~100.2s | TLS session to `business.checkfedexexp.com` (172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70) — same phishing-kit infrastructure |
| 135.94s | `HEAD /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` to raw IP **72.5.43.29:80** |
| 136.16s | `GET /data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` → downloads a Windows x64 PE32+ DLL (159,232 bytes) |
| 196.86s → 1962.0s (end of capture) | Continuous beaconing (305× GET, 3× POST, 1× HEAD) to 72.5.43.29:80, still active when the capture ends |

## 4. Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint (confirmed active, ongoing at capture end):**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — plain HTTP, no domain used (hardcoded IP). Beacon requests use `User-Agent: Mozilla / 5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` (note the anomalous space in "Mozilla / 5.0" — a spoofed/legacy UA out of place on a modern Win10/11 host) and a large base64 value in a `Cookie:` header carrying what appears to be an encrypted session token. Server responses are a mix of HTTP 200 (32-byte binary body) and HTTP 400 Bad Request.

**Malicious/phishing domains:**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 104.21.55.70 / 172.67.170.159, Cloudflare-fronted)
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` (resolves to 172.67.170.159 / 104.21.55.70)

**Malicious URL (initial delivery):**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215`

**Malicious payload URL (loader download):**
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`

**Transferred files and hashes:**

| Filename | Type | Size | SHA256 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Invoice 876597035_003.zip` | ZIP container | 2,767,804 bytes | not separately hashed (ZIP wrapper); contains item below |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | Obfuscated JScript downloader (padded with ~4MB of decoy academic-text content and dead-code injection to inflate size/evade static AV scanning) | 6,990,020 bytes | **dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c** |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` (served path `/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`) | Windows x64 PE32+ DLL (loader/backdoor, PDB `knock_v1.1.8\knock\bin64\knock.pdb`, exports `release.dll`; imports include `ADVAPI32.dll`, `WS2_32.dll`, `SHELL32.dll`, `ole32.dll`, `CreateThread`) | 159,232 bytes | **b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6** |

## 5. Notes / Caveats

- One artifact thread was investigated and discarded: files apparently referencing a second C2 (`5.252.153.241`) and PowerShell scripts (`29842.ps1`, `pas.ps1`) turned up in a `tshark --export-objects` output directory, but their file timestamps predated this analysis session and `5.252.153.241` does not appear anywhere in this pcap — these were stale leftovers from an unrelated prior task in the same temp directory, not evidence from this capture. They are excluded from the IOC list above.
- All other traffic to Microsoft/Adobe/Bing/MSN/Office/BITS delivery endpoints observed in the capture is consistent with normal Windows/Edge telemetry and update activity and is not treated as malicious.
